record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and listed result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal outcomes for endpoints described as abliterated and compares them with a stock Kimi-K3 endpoint. This benchmarks the practical outcome named by V2, but does not perform or isolate the weight edit.
record.gate_note: The repo is a measurement tool, not a refusal-direction intervention. It reports outcomes for endpoints labelled abliterated, including regex and LLM-judge refusal measures, and a stock endpoint comparator. It does not find, remove, or add a residual-stream direction; nor does it test attacks, robustness training, harmfulness judgments as a separate representation, or general capability.
record.test_reason: An outcome benchmark of deployed endpoints described as abliterated or derisked. It reports their refusal rates on 519–520 AdvBench-style prompts, with a stock Kimi-K3 endpoint as comparator. The results bear on V2's practical claim in a new setting (commercial serving), but the edit procedure is never verified. It does not test V1 or V3–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also claim the serving stack rather than the weights sets refusal, saying every endpoint serves Kimi-K3. Their own comparison, though, pits stock against derisked weights (97.5% vs ~3%), so that claim mixes weight and serving effects. They also say abliterated endpoints mostly fail by deflecting rather than refusing.
record.recipe_differences: This is a refusal measurement benchmark, not a replication or application of the original activation-difference direction method. It evaluates deployed endpoints described as abliterated; it does not perform a direction ablation or weight edit.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports serving-stack differences, run-to-run variation, judge-versus-regex differences, and differences associated with reasoning configuration. Two runs of the same endpoint differed on 19/520 prompts despite similar aggregate rates; the judge and regex also produce substantially different compliance estimates.

fits_no_version.finding: The same abliterated Kimi-K3 checkpoint gives 15.0% judge refusal in a two-stage thinker+answerer pipeline versus 5.8% single-stage. Regex and judge rankings of endpoints can invert.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal in abliterated models depends on serving configuration (multi-stage pipelines, reasoning effort, quantisation) and on the refusal classifier, not only on the weight edit.

record.problems: No matched before/after weight-edit test or independently verified edit procedure is reported. The README notes that the regex classifier is phrasing-based and can misclassify deflections and refusals; the LLM judge is self-judged for one Kimi-K3 result. It also notes endpoint nondeterminism and ambiguous empty responses. No general-capability assessment is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported refusal-rate results were intentionally omitted from the README's result tables. Results for additional deployment variants described only by aggregate delivery/deflection without a refusal measure were not added as separate rows unless the README gave an explicit refusal rate.

untested.parts: Whether the endpoints were actually produced by a direction-ablation weight edit (procedure unverified). Matched before/after tests, except stock vs derisked Kimi-K3. Retention of other abilities. Released models other than Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3 and Qwen3.8.
All; no direction is computed, ablated or added.
All; reasoning endpoints are benchmarked, but no direction intervention is made on them.

Only the Kimi-K3 rows have a stock baseline, and that baseline is scored by regex only. The record's 'challenges' label on r7 was wrong: a stock model refusing is the expected baseline, not evidence against V2.

source_check.notes: The source is a vendor README advertising its own uncensored endpoints. The 'Audn Abliteration'/'derisked' procedure is not described, checkpoint identities are self-reported, and the KIMI-K3-1M judge run is self-judged. FINDINGS.md is not in the text. The stock baseline D is regex-only. The README's claim that 'every endpoint serves Kimi-K3' is contradicted by Qwen3.8 rows in the same table. Unrowed judge results exist (Warlock GLM 5.3: 7.5% refused / 10% deflected; k3-2leg-venice 18.8% refused; Omen 17.4%).

statements.correction: Kimi-K3 abliterated endpoints, regex: refusal 0.2-3.3% (effective incl. empties 2.9-6.5%); stock Kimi-K3 (D) 97.5%. GLM-5.3 NVFP4 regex refusal 7.7%. LLM-judge explicit refusal: standard two-stage necromicon 15.0% (78/520), whose regex comply on the same pipeline is 96.7%; KIMI-K3-1M 5.8%; GLM-5.3 builds 1.0-6.0%. Judge deflection 17.5-22.8%; delivered 65.0-79.1%.
statements.problem: '1-6.5% explicit refusal by regex' mixes measures: 1.0%, 1.1% and 6.0% are LLM-judge figures for GLM-5.3 builds, and 6.5% is effective refusal (regex plus empties). The 15.0% judge refusal holds only for the standard two-stage pipeline, but the statement reads as general.

statements.correction: Regex refusal on abliterated Kimi-K3 endpoints 0.2-3.3% (effective 2.9-6.5%). LLM-judge explicit refusal 1.0-15.0% (GLM-5.3 1.0-6.0%, KIMI-K3-1M 5.8%, standard two-stage pipeline 15.0%). LLM-judge deflection 17.5-22.8%.
statements.problem: The point (explicit refusal vs deflection) is right, but '1-6.5% regex' is not a regex range: its low end (1.0-1.1%) is LLM-judge refusal on GLM-5.3 builds, and 6.5% is effective refusal including silent empties.
